sets.relationshipLabel: a theatrical genre and its most iconic work
sets.explanation: Each genre is paired with the single work most people would name first if asked for an example.

sets.relationshipLabel: a theatre worker and the material their work is centered on
sets.explanation: Costume designers work in wardrobe and dramaturgs work in script, each defined by the object their craft revolves around rather than a tool they wield.

sets.relationshipLabel: a condition that lets a stage event happen unseen
sets.explanation: A blackout hides a scene change and a harness hides the mechanics of a flying effect, both concealing the means behind the moment.

sets.relationshipLabel: the first and last moment marking a theatrical span
sets.explanation: Casting opens and strike closes a production's life, just as the overture opens and the encore closes a single performance.

glossary.definition: A theater specialist who researches and advises on a play's history, structure, and meaning.

definitions.definition: A serious story where things end badly for the main character, often through fate or flaws.
A famous play about a prince wrestling with revenge, grief, and doubt.
A show where the story is told partly through songs and dance.
A long-running show about a tribe of cats who sing and dance through the night.
The person who creates and plans what every performer wears on stage.
All the clothes and costumes used in a production.
A theater specialist who researches and advises on a play's history, structure, and meaning.
The written text of a play, with all the lines and stage directions.
A moment when all the stage lights go completely dark.
The shift from one setting or scene to another during a show.
A strapped rig worn by a performer to keep them safe while suspended or moved.
A stage illusion that makes a performer appear to soar or float through the air.
The process of choosing which actors will play which roles.
The final teardown of a set once a show has finished its run.
The instrumental music played before a show officially begins.
An extra bit of performance given after the show ends, by audience demand.
